headline: The Memphis City Council delayed a vote on a one-year pause on new data centres, and the meeting turned chaotic.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered to 5: the vote happened on 6 Oct 2026, before 7 Oct, so the item is stale; the report was read in full and nothing is overstated.
importance_line: The vote is now set for 20 Oct, so the pause is still open, which matters to Memphis residents worried about power, water and air quality, while opponents such as Councilman Jeff Warren argue it could push companies to nearby counties.
summary: Fox News reports that the Memphis City Council voted 7-5 on Tuesday night, 6 Oct 2026, to put off until 20 Oct a vote on a 12-month pause on new data centres, meant to give the city time to study their effects on health and on Memphis's power, water and other infrastructure. Police cleared protesters from the chamber and a fight followed in the lobby, though police said no one was detained or hurt.
